描述_ZN: The Flower Album, Ming Dynasty, painted by Wen, on paper with color, each opening 27.8 cm in length and 42.8 cm in width.　　The book is composed of eight panels, depicting flowers such as begonias, gypsophila, wild chrysanthemums, and gladioli, either with folded branches or lined with lake rocks and pink butterflies, paying attention to the differences in composition between them, and the layout is quite elaborate. The branches, leaves and petals of the flowers in the picture are mostly stained with no bones, without outlining the outer outline, and the leaves and petals are outlined with fine lines inside their veins and veins, with attention to the fine staining of the colors, which are bright and elegant. At the same time, the painter also pays attention to choosing different expression techniques according to the different objects depicted, such as the leaves and petals in the picture of Jianlan, which are all outlined with thin and strong lines. The lake rocks in the picture are also represented by the boneless method, first using light ink to stain them, then reminding them of their structure with wet thick ink, and finally using dry ink to slightly outline the outer contours. Although the painting style of Wen Bian is more refined and meticulous, his emphasis on coloring techniques and his clean and elegant style are derived from Wen Zhengming. There is a postscript of Liu Zhisi on the back of the album.　　Inscriptions by the author include "Seal of Wen Bian" in white, "Wen Duanrong's" in white, "Wen Bian" in white, "Duanrong The author's seals include "Seal of Wen Bian" in white, "Wen Duanrong's" in white, "Wen Bian" in white, "Duanrong" in white, "Duan Cai" in white, "Duan Cai" in white, "Duan Cai" in white, "Duan Rong" in white, and "Duan Cai has a trace, and Duan Cai has a leisure" in vermilion, "Juxue xuan thing" seal in white, "Liu Zhisi" seal in white, "Gong Lu" seal in vermilion, "Lan Yi Yu Du" seal in vermilion, etc. vermilion seal, etc. On the bottom right of the page of "Sword and Orchid", there is the artist's self-title: "Xinwei in the tenth and second month of the year, Tianshui Zhao's Wen Bian painted." Xinwei was the fourth year of Chongzhen of Ming Dynasty (1631), and the artist was 37 years old.
